newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-BUDGET REVENUE UP, BUT SHORT OF TARGET.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-BUDGET REVENUE UP, BUT SHORT OF TARGET.

text.p: Lithuania collected 100.8 million litas less in budget revenues than it expected in January and February, a parliamentary finance and budget committe official said.

"Lithuania has collected 752.5 million litas in January and February 1997 versus 853.3 million litas planned for the period," the deputy chairman of parliament's finance and budget committee, Kestutis Glaveckas, told Reuters.
Glaveckas said the government had collected 126.3 million litas more during the first two months of the year against the same 1996 period.
"The situation with budget revenues is better than in 1996 but it is still not good enough to carry out the state's obligations for this year," he added.
Lithuania's centre-right government planned to collect 6.02 billion litas revenues in 1997, when it expects to have a budget deficit of 698 million litas.
